issues.description: IAM policy fetch failures are silently treated as 'not publicly shared', producing false PASS findings
issues.detail: When getIamPolicy raises (e.g., permission denied as in test-image-3), the except logs and leaves publicly_shared=False, so the image is reported as PASS despite its IAM state being unknown. For a security check, unknown state must not be reported as compliant. Skip the image, mark it MANUAL, or surface the error instead.

issues.description: PR title/description reference a different check name than the code (compute_image_publicly_shared vs compute_image_not_publicly_shared)
issues.detail: The directory, class, metadata CheckID, and CHANGELOG entry all use compute_image_not_publicly_shared, while the PR title and description say compute_image_publicly_shared. Reconcile docs, PR description, and the metadata Recommendation.Url (hub.prowler.com link) before merge to avoid broken references.

issues.description: _get_images runs sequentially per project instead of using __threading_call__ like every other collector
issues.detail: All other resource fetchers in compute_service.py use __threading_call__ across projects/regions/zones, but _get_images iterates project_ids serially and makes one getIamPolicy call per image sequentially. On accounts with many projects/images this materially slows scans and breaks the established pattern. Parallelize across project_ids.

issues.description: Required compute.images.getIamPolicy permission not added to provider permission docs
issues.detail: The check newly invokes images().getIamPolicy, which requires the compute.images.getIamPolicy IAM permission not in the standard viewer role. The PR checklist flags permission review, but no permission/role manifest was updated. Without this, scans will silently log permission errors and pass everything, compounding the false-negative issue above.

issues.description: Image listing does not filter deprecated or non-custom images
issues.detail: images().list(project=project_id) returns all project-owned images including deprecated ones. The description claims only 'custom images' are evaluated, but there is no filter on deprecated.state and intentionally-public publisher images would fail. Either filter (e.g., deprecated.state!=DEPRECATED) or document the scope.

issues.description: Image model is too thin — boolean-only loses role/member context useful for findings
issues.detail: The Image model only stores name, id, project_id, and publicly_shared, discarding which roles/members triggered the public binding. Other compute resources store richer context, and status_extended/remediation cannot cite specifics without it. Consider adding self_link/family and the offending bindings list.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the check is small, well-structured, and well-tested in the happy path, but has one significant correctness gap: when getIamPolicy fails (e.g., permission denied), the image is silently recorded as publicly_shared=False and reported as PASS, turning unknown IAM state into a clean bill of health — and the existing test for image-3 codifies this silent-failure behavior. The new compute.images.getIamPolicy permission requirement is not reflected in provider permission docs, which will compound the false-negative in default deployments. _get_images also skips the __threading_call__ pattern used by every other compute collector, serializing per-project and per-image API calls. Finally, the PR description/title reference compute_image_publicly_shared while the code/CHANGELOG/metadata use compute_image_not_publicly_shared — reconcile before merge.
